title: Di Resta wins from pole at Hockenheim as Glock is disqualified
dek: Paul di Resta led from pole to win Sunday's one-hour race for Mercedes, with BMW's Farfus and Martin promoted to the podium after Timo Glock's post-race disqualification and Paffett's drive-through.

chapters.title: Audi's Saturday, and a gearbox change in the night
text: Saturday had belonged to Audi. Edoardo Mortara won the opening race from second on the grid, Nico Müller took a first podium from pole, and Mortara went into Sunday leading the championship on 25 points from Robert Wickens on 18 and Müller on 15. But the race had cost seven cars, and the balance between the makes on Sunday was anyone's guess. Di Resta's team, meanwhile, had to change the gearbox on his Mercedes overnight.

chapters.title: Di Resta on pole, with no Audi in the top ten
text: The order from Saturday was turned upside down. Paul di Resta took pole for the second race with a 1m34.060s, despite the overnight gearbox change, and said that the car had been fast all weekend and that a podium must now be the minimum aim. Augusto Farfus was 0.126 seconds behind in the best BMW, and Gary Paffett was third for the ART Mercedes squad, 0.138 seconds off, saying afterwards that he could have challenged di Resta had he put his lap together.

Maxime Martin and Robert Wickens shared the same 1m34.285s for fourth and fifth, 0.225 seconds from pole. Timo Glock, Esteban Ocon, Tom Blomqvist, Marco Wittmann and António Félix da Costa completed the top ten, which contained six BMWs and four Mercedes, and not a single Audi. Jamie Green was the best of the four-ringed cars in 11th, 0.391 seconds off, ahead of Saturday's winner Mortara in 12th. Müller was 15th, Lucas Auer 16th, and Miguel Molina last of the 24 cars, 1.095 seconds behind di Resta, which was the full spread of the field.

chapters.title: A three-car crash brings out the safety car
text: Di Resta made a perfect start from pole and was already a few seconds clear when the race was neutralised. Ocon, Green and Bruno Spengler collided in the first lap, and all three were out on the spot, which brought the safety car out almost immediately. Spengler was furious with the rookie at first, but after seeing the television pictures both he and the stewards concluded that it was a normal racing accident, and he later apologised for his outburst.

At the restart Paffett, who had started third, moved into second place and set about chasing di Resta, and the Mercedes pair were soon clear of the BMWs of Farfus and Glock. Of the leading drivers, Paffett was the only one who looked able to match the pace of the leader.

chapters.title: Di Resta survives a slow stop, Paffett is penalised
text: The stops almost turned the race. Di Resta's was slow because of a problem with his right-front tyre, and it looked as though Paffett would take the lead, but the Scot just held on while the ART driver struggled in traffic. Minutes later Paffett's own chance was gone. He was given a drive-through penalty for an unsafe release in the pit lane and rejoined deep in the pack.

With Paffett out of the way, di Resta pulled away from Farfus and Glock, who had worked past the Brazilian for second place. Retirements thinned the field as the race went on: da Costa stopped after 11 laps, Mattias Ekström after 16, Timo Scheider after 18, Molina after 22 and Daniel Juncadella after 29. Paffett meanwhile charged back through the field and was within reach of the podium places at the flag.

chapters.title: Di Resta wins by more than 13 seconds
text: Di Resta took the flag after 37 laps in 1:01:42.654, his first DTM win since 2010, and he was well clear. Glock crossed the line second, but several hours after the race he was excluded when measurements showed that the rear lid on his BMW did not meet the specification. That promoted Farfus to second, 13.905 seconds behind the winner, and Martin to third, with Paffett fourth, 15.055 seconds back, having finished just behind the BMWs on the road.

Wickens was fifth and Blomqvist sixth, Müller seventh as the best Audi, Wittmann eighth, Tomczyk ninth and Mike Rockenfeller tenth. Mortara was out of the points in 11th. Four Audis failed to finish, and Lucas Auer, who was classified in 15th, was two laps down.

chapters.title: Di Resta takes the lead, BMW gets a double podium after Glock's exclusion
text: Di Resta said it had been a long time since he had last stood on top of the podium, and that his win owed everything to his mechanics, who had worked through the night on the gearbox change and finished at around half past five in the morning. His last victory had come in October 2010, in the season in which he won the title, and he said it had taken longer than he had hoped since he came back to the DTM from Formula 1. The result put him in front of the championship with 37 points.

For BMW the afternoon had a bitter end. Glock was delighted with the pace of the car, a good start and a fair fight with Wickens, and spoke of having only one chance to get past Farfus before taking it. He lost the place when the disqualification came, and the double podium went to Farfus and Martin instead. Farfus said the team had lacked a bit of pace but that BMW had still collected many points. Even without Glock, five BMWs finished in the top ten, a sign that the concessions granted to the make for 2016 had given the M4 a fair chance.

Paffett was angry at the lost chance, saying that he had one of the fastest cars of the day and that fifth place on the road after a drive-through was disappointing. Audi, which had four cars in the top five of the grid on Saturday, had no car in the top ten of qualifying, lost four cars before the flag and took points only with Müller and Rockenfeller. The drivers had put Saturday's many crashes down to the seven-month break, but the first lap of Sunday's race brought another, and Spengler's apology to Ocon for his radio outburst was the lasting image of it.

In the standings di Resta led with 37 points from Wickens on 28 and Mortara on 25, with Müller on 21, Martin on 19 and Farfus on 18. Mortara, who had left Saturday as leader, slipped to third after his 11th place. The championship moved on two weeks later to the Red Bull Ring in Austria for the second weekend of the season.

facts.v: Paul di Resta won from pole in 1:01:42.654, his first DTM win since October 2010, and took the championship lead.
